latin: Haec est in quarto modo dicendi per se: homo est homo.
translation: This belongs to the fourth mode of speaking per se: man is man.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch1, from Latin at farmer1998:10933

sources.text: Aristotle, Posterior Analytics 1.4 (commentary tradition on the four modes of per se predication)
sources.pico_relation: Farmer traces the scholastic background of the fourth mode of per se predication to this text

doctrine: The thesis classifies the proposition 'man is man' as belonging to the fourth of the modes in which a predicate is ascribed to a subject per se (farmer1998:10933). Farmer's note traces the four modes to the commentary tradition on the Posterior Analytics 1.4 (farmer1998:11013). The same note cross-refers the fourth mode to a thesis on common sensibles and to three of Pico's own theses on the common sense and reason (farmer1998:11130).
historiography: Edelheit's chapter states that thesis 3 places the proposition 'a human being is a human being' in the fourth mode of speaking per se, and that Albert discusses the four modes in his commentary on the Posterior Analytics, book 1, tract 2, chapter 8 (edelheit2022:9242). Edelheit reports that in this fourth mode the proposition does not depend on anything else (edelheit2022:9267).
not_established: Context and reception beyond Edelheit's citation are not established by the sources consulted.
